hypotheses.claim: Under a 500 ms per-instance budget on tsp_guided_insertion_2opt, replacing a single greedy cheapest-insertion + full-matrix 2-opt sweep with (a) regret-2 guided insertion over a k-nearest-neighbor candidate set and (b) first-improvement 2-opt restricted to those candidate lists, plus seed restarts, yields a shorter final tour length than the plain insertion/2-opt baseline while staying inside the deterministic time budget, because candidate-list restriction cuts per-move cost so many more improving moves are evaluated per millisecond.

next_search_advice.direction: Use budget-adaptive construction (regret-2 / nearest-neighbor-guided insertion with k-nearest candidate seeding) followed by first-improvement 2-opt over truncated neighbor lists (k≈16-20), restarting construction from a different seed while time budget remains, so 500 ms is spent on repeated cheap improvement rather than one expensive full pass.
